text: Terror was upon her white face as she saw it; her cheek was flaccid, and her mouth had almost the aspect of a round little hole. The horrible sense of his view of her so deadened her that she staggered, and he stepped forward, thinking she was going to fall. “Sit down, sit down,” he said gently. “You are ill; and it is natural that you should be.” She did sit down, without knowing where she was, that strained look still upon her face, and her eyes such as to make his flesh creep. “I don’t belong to you any more, then; do I, Angel?” she asked helplessly.
